title: Config synthesis layer for multi-mode rollouts
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Build a lightweight config synthesis layer that translates a single high-level rollout spec into environment-specific deployment manifests for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes. The layer will enforce environment constraints (networking, KMS access, kernel/quantization compatibility, capacity limits) and produce a validated plan for canary, A/B, and shadow experiments plus an automated rollback policy. It intentionally avoids creating a third canonical runtime; instead we synthesize and validate concrete configs and run a simulation to detect mismatches before execution.
acceptance_criteria: High-level rollout spec input accepted by API/console and stored as a single source-of-truth
Translation engine outputs environment-specific manifests (hosted, dedicated, private) and flags constraint violations
Simulator can run a rollout dry-run and produce latency/cost/error delta estimates for each environment
Rollout planner supports weighted A/B, phased canaries, and shadow mirroring with per-environment limits
Auto-rollback policy implemented as a pluggable guard with circuit-breaker thresholds (p50/p95 latency, error-rate, token-cost deviation)
End-to-end tests covering a hosted canary, a dedicated A/B, and a private shadow run with a validated rollback
Console UX surfaces synthesized diffs and a one-click approve/apply flow
Security review completed and Private mode KMS/HSM access patterns documented

comments: 2025-11-04 - Kickoff: Aligned on single-source rollout spec to avoid dual-maintenance between modes. Decision: synthesize concrete configs instead of forcing a new canonical runtime.
2025-11-06 - Design review: PMs requested explicit cost delta estimates per environment; added simulator task. Design doc uploaded: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DO/Config+Synthesis+Layer

2025-11-08 - Security: Private deployments cannot assume outbound KMS access. Added KMS integration patterns (HSM proxy or customer-managed KMS endpoint) and marked ticket security_review_required=true.

2025-11-09 - Engineering: Early prototype translates canary weights and capacity hints into Dedicated GPU pool reservations. Found gap: Dedicated autoscale window semantics differ from Hosted; added translation rule to map 'target-rps' into 'reserved-instances' heuristics.

2025-11-10 - Trade-offs: We considered forcing identical feature parity across environments but chose to synthesize and document environment-specific fallbacks to reduce friction and avoid regression risk in Private air-gapped installs.

2025-11-11 - PR opened for translation core: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1427. Initial tests show simulation latency deltas are within 10% of production traces for short sequences.

2025-11-12 - Design feedback from Console team: need a clear diffs view that highlights 'unsupported' config items in Private and suggested automated mappings. Sophia iterating on mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/console-config-diffs
